causes.cause: the sheet turned past edge-on to the plane
causes.plain: 19% of the paper faces away from the plane. Where the sheet turns past edge-on, the part beyond is dropped back over the part before it, so two layers land on the same spots.

causes.cause: the plane shortens tilted parts of the sheet
causes.plain: Nothing folds, but dropping points straight onto a plane shortens any part of the sheet tilted away from it. Typical tilted part keeps 73% of its area and the most tilted keeps 49%, so the result cannot be the original square.

causes.plain: 12 of 42250 neighbour links join parts of the sheet that are far apart on the paper but close in 3D. Every walk that uses one takes a shortcut through the air, so one bad link corrupts many distances. The same layout step passes when given perfect neighbours, so the hops are what went wrong.
